summary: DSpark compact verification now lets a forced SPS profiling budget bypass the uninitialized-table verify-all cache, while preserving that cache for startup and normal no-table serving. Speculative mRoPE construction now maps packed ragged tokens to request-specific deltas through the QO indptr and leaves CUDA Graph tail padding at zero.

tests.what_was_measured: Pre-fix regression: the forced budget never reached _schedule_verify_lens, and packed mRoPE positions assigned incorrect per-request deltas and nonzero graph padding. Both tests failed before the production changes.
Post-fix focused DSpark scheduler and ragged verification suite: 37 tests and 18 subtests passed.

Actual ForwardBatch.compute_spec_mrope_positions execution on AMD Instinct MI355X for batch_size=48, graph_tokens=640, real_tokens=575 and padding_tokens=65. Compared with an independently constructed CPU row-by-row reference; output shape was (3, 640) and max absolute error was 0.
All applicable repository formatting, lint, spelling, and registered-test validation hooks passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 reported one AMD Instinct MI355X. The 48-request, 640-token mRoPE check executed tensors and searchsorted on cuda:0, synchronized successfully, and matched the independent CPU reference exactly.

remaining_limitations: The full two-GPU Qwen DSpark profiling server from the NVIDIA H20 report was not run: this prepared environment exposes one AMD MI355X and does not provide the reported model checkpoints. The planner profiling contract and the reported 48-request/640-token positional shape were exercised directly through their production methods. No native C++ or FlyDSL files were changed, so no native rebuild was applicable. Source paths: python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_planner.py and python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py. Native paths: none. Raw validation output is retained in reports/j-d0964f71c779/validation.txt.
